data: Is the value of the red dot representing 1900-1920 on the line in the top plot higher than the value of the red dot representing 1900-1920 on the line in the bottom plot?

The question asks whether the value of the red dot representing 1900-1920 on the line in the top plot is higher than the value of the red dot representing 1900-1920 on the line in the bottom plot. 

From the caption, we know that the top plot represents the Merging Index and the bottom plot represents the Splitting Index. The red dots represent the values for the 1900-1920 period.

Looking at the top plot, the red dot for the 1900-1920 period is approximately 0.84. Looking at the bottom plot, the red dot for the 1900-1920 period is also approximately 0.84.

Comparing these two values, they appear to be equal. Therefore, the value of the red dot representing 1900-1920 on the line in the top plot is not higher than the value of the red dot representing 1900-1920 on the line in the bottom plot. They are equal.
